checks.name: Accepted Profile flow-policy vocabulary and ranges are mirrored exactly
checks.method: read `xdl/profiles/xcom-v0.1.schema.json` `$defs/flowPolicy` and compared field-by-field with contract.hpp:52-104 (enumerations), contract.hpp:281-285 (bounds), and contract.cpp:202-244 (`to_string` text)
checks.result: pass: ordering {fifo, priority, unordered}, reliability {at-most-once, at-least-once, exactly-once, best-effort}, and overflow {drop-oldest, drop-newest, coalesce, lossless-backpressure, reject, fail-closed} match the Profile enums verbatim through the `to_string` external text; deadlineMs 0-600000, retry 0-64, and queueDepth 1-65536 match the inclusive Profile minimum/maximum exactly. No value the Profile rejects is accepted and no Profile value is missing (T013-SR-007).

checks.name: Immutability, value and ownership semantics, and thread safety
checks.method: read contract.hpp:278-345 (FlowPolicy), result.hpp, the `static_assert`s in unit_tests.cpp:337-340, and the baseline `test_concurrent_const_reads`
checks.result: pass: FlowPolicy exposes const accessors only, defaults a `noexcept` copy constructor, deletes copy assignment, holds six trivially copyable value members, and shares no mutable state, so concurrent const reads are safe. The test asserts copy-constructible, not copy-assignable, nothrow copy-constructible, `noexcept(FlowPolicy::create(...))`, and copy invariance. `Result<T>` (result.hpp) holds exactly one value or one non-empty DiagnosticSet and deletes assignment, so a returned accessor cannot be invalidated (T013-SR-010).

checks.name: Failure atomicity and rejected-operation side effects
checks.method: read contract.cpp:277-310 (FlowPolicy::create), contract.cpp:26-55 (DiagnosticAccumulator), and the new negative tests
checks.result: pass: create validates all six fields into a call-local accumulator and only constructs a FlowPolicy after the `diagnostics.empty()` guard, so a rejected declaration yields `Result<FlowPolicy>::failure(*set)` with a non-empty sorted DiagnosticSet and constructs no value. The input is taken by `const&` and only read; no allocation, I/O, or caller-state mutation occurs; no factory overload supplies a default, and `operator==` compares every declared field, so a weaker declaration is never silently upgraded (T013-SR-005/006). The negative tests assert `!has_value()`, `value() == nullptr`, `diagnostics() != nullptr`, and an exact per-case diagnostic count.

checks.name: Diagnostic bounds and compatibility of existing codes, phases, and ordering
checks.method: read diagnostic.hpp:24-126 and diagnostic.hpp:226, diagnostic.cpp:33-77 (known_code/known_phase), diagnostic.cpp:147-213 (`to_string`), and the contract.cpp accumulator signature change; grepped the tree for `XCOM-TYPE-E006` and for switches over DiagnosticCode/ValidationPhase
checks.result: pass: DiagnosticCode::invalid_policy (diagnostic.hpp:39) and ValidationPhase::policy (diagnostic.hpp:56) are appended after every existing enumerator, so no existing enumerator value, code text, phase text, ordering key, or bound changes. `XCOM-TYPE-E006` is 14 bytes and unique (existing `XCOM-LIFE-E006` has different full text); `policy` is 6 bytes, within the unchanged kMaximumPhaseBytes = 23 (diagnostic.hpp:116). kMaximumCodeBytes = 14, kMaximumDiagnostics = 32, and kMaximumTextBytes = 256 are unchanged; the eight existing phases and the TYPE-E001..E005 / LIFE-E006..E013 code set are intact. The only exhaustive switches over these enums both cover the new values, so `-Wswitch -Werror` remains clean.

checks.name: Determinism and byte-stable diagnostic ordering
checks.method: read diagnostic.cpp:242-298 (Diagnostic::create, DiagnosticSet::create_from_inputs, sort_initialized), negative_tests.cpp:416-443, and unit_tests.cpp:336-396
checks.result: pass: diagnostics sort by the escaped `phase|severity|code|affected_identity|reason|correction` key independent of insertion order. `test_flow_policy_exact_diagnostics` asserts the exact two- and three-violation byte sequences; `test_flow_policy_immutability_and_determinism` feeds the same five invalid_policy inputs forward and reverse and asserts byte-identical `serialize()` plus equality with the actual `FlowPolicy::create` failure (T013-SR-008/009).

checks.name: Correlation and time behaviour unchanged and free of cross-clock inference
checks.method: inspected item.hpp:65-71, item.hpp:124-131, item.hpp:198-201 and value.hpp Timestamp; compared against requirements.md T013-SR-012 and detailed-design.md section 3.2
checks.result: pass: item.hpp is unmodified by the candidate and retains one signed Timestamp magnitude plus one explicit clock-domain Identity, with no cross-domain ordering or comparison API; Accessors return the magnitude without inference. requirements.md T013-SR-012 and detailed-design.md section 3.2 describe exactly this behaviour, and NEG-19 records the absence of any cross-clock API.

checks.name: Policy validation precedence, bounded diagnostics, and finite resources
checks.method: read contract.cpp:277-310 and contract.cpp:52, cross-checked the fixed validation order and the accumulator capacity against detailed-design.md section 4.3/section 7 and requirements.md T013-SR-011
checks.result: pass: create validates in the fixed order ordering, reliability, overflow, deadline_ms, retry, queue_depth, emitting at most one invalid_policy diagnostic per field (at most six). The accumulator is `std::array<DiagnosticInput, 6U>` (contract.cpp:52), so the maximum write index is 5 and no out-of-bounds write is reachable at this revision. deadline_ms/retry/queue_depth are finite declared ranges; no unbounded queue, quota, retry, or depth exists. The declaration type enforces nothing at runtime (T013-LIM-03), which is the intended declaration-only scope.

checks.method: read every added case in unit_tests.cpp:235-409 and negative_tests.cpp:358-451; diffed both files against the baseline; compared `ctest -N`; rebuilt and ran the executables and the full suite
checks.result: pass: `test_flow_policy_table` round-trips all 72 declared enum combinations with exact external text; `test_flow_policy_boundaries` accepts each minimum and maximum and rejects each one-step neighbour with one invalid_policy diagnostic; `test_flow_policy_rejections` covers one unknown enum per vocabulary and each out-of-range numeric field; `test_flow_policy_immutability_and_determinism` covers copy invariance, no-upgrade, and order independence; `test_flow_policy_exact_diagnostics` asserts exact failure bytes. notes.summary: `DiagnosticAccumulator::add` appends with an unchecked `inputs_[size_++]` into a fixed six-slot array; the safety margin is exactly zero because the policy path can legitimately emit all six diagnostics.
notes.evidence: src/xverse/xcom/src/contract.cpp:39 writes `inputs_[size_++]` with no capacity guard, and src/xverse/xcom/src/contract.cpp:52 declares `std::array<DiagnosticInput, 6U> inputs_{}`. `FlowPolicy::create` (src/xverse/xcom/src/contract.cpp:277-307) can emit exactly six diagnostics (three vocabulary checks plus three range checks), so the maximum write index is 5 and no overflow is reachable at this revision; the same holds for the six-call `CommunicationContract::create` (src/xverse/xcom/src/contract.cpp:246-259).
notes.required_correction: If a later slice adds a seventh policy field or another contract validator, raise the array capacity or add an explicit `size_ < inputs_.size()` guard before the write, in that owning task's pass; T013 must not be changed for this observation.
notes.closure_test: Static inspection that the accumulator capacity is greater than or equal to the maximum number of add/validate call sites on every path that constructs it; the unmutated T013 candidate must still build warning-clean and pass `ctest --test-dir build/fabro-t013 --output-on-failure` with 248/248.

notes.summary: `FlowPolicy::create` dereferences the `std::optional<DiagnosticSet>` returned by `DiagnosticSet::create_from_inputs` without a null check, which is safe only because the internally generated inputs are guaranteed valid.
notes.evidence: src/xverse/xcom/src/contract.cpp:304-306 does `const auto set = DiagnosticSet::create_from_inputs(diagnostics.inputs()); return Result<FlowPolicy>::failure(*set);`. `create_from_inputs` (src/xverse/xcom/src/diagnostic.cpp:269-285) returns `std::nullopt` only for an empty/over-capacity span or an invalid input; the six fixed policy inputs use short bounded text and known code/phase, so it always yields a value here. The identical pattern already exists in the baseline `CommunicationContract::create` (src/xverse/xcom/src/contract.cpp:261-264).
notes.required_correction: None required for T013, consistent with the accepted baseline pattern and unreachable. If a later hardening pass adopts defensive optional handling, apply it uniformly to both factories in that owning task.
notes.closure_test: Inspection that every reachable diagnostic-input path stays within kMaximumDiagnostics and uses valid bounded text so create_from_inputs cannot return an empty optional; T013's negative tests already exercise the failure branch and pass.
